claims.text: The homogenized Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is a single-phase solid solution in its solidified initial state.
The dynamic strength–ductility balance of Co-free FeNiCrMn is controlled by short-range chemical order.
Temperature modulates the effectiveness of short-range chemical order as a barrier to dislocation motion.
Strain rate modulates the effectiveness of short-range chemical order as a barrier to dislocation motion.
At lower temperatures, short-range order more effectively impedes dislocation motion.
At lower strain rates, short-range order more effectively impedes dislocation motion.
More effective short-range-order barriers increase yield strength and reduce ductility.
At elevated temperatures, thermal activation or dynamic recovery reduces the barrier to dislocation motion imposed by short-range order.
At higher strain rates, thermal activation or dynamic recovery reduces the barrier to dislocation motion imposed by short-range order.
Reduction of the short-range-order barrier lowers yield strength and enhances ductility.
Under conditions where short-range order strongly constrains dislocations, Co-free FeNiCrMn will have higher yield strength than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi tested under identical conditions.
Under conditions where short-range order strongly constrains dislocations, Co-free FeNiCrMn will have lower ductility than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi tested under identical conditions.
Increasing temperature or strain rate so that the short-range-order effect diminishes will shift Co-free FeNiCrMn toward lower yield strength.
Increasing temperature or strain rate so that the short-range-order effect diminishes will shift Co-free FeNiCrMn toward improved ductility.

The proposed mechanism applies from approximately 25°C to 600°C and from approximately 10^-3 s^-1 to 10^3 s^-1, provided that the alloy remains a single-phase solid solution without phase transformations.
Microstructural variability and secondary deformation mechanisms may alter the quantitative strength and ductility differences between the alloys.
